problem: Find the particular solution to the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x-2y}$ that satisfies $y(0)=0.$

feedback.worked_solution:
We split the integral into the difference of two integrals and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}(x-\frac{2}{1+{x}^{2}})\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x-2{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{1}{1+{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1}+2\,\text{arccot}\,x\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({1}^{2}-{0}^{2})+2(\text{arccot}(1)-\text{arccot}(0)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+2(\frac{\pi }{4}-\frac{\pi }{2}) \\  & =-\frac{\pi }{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
